title: Settings or development: hand over a testable requirement
goal: Separate correcting a filter from adding report behavior and specify a verifiable engineering task.
prerequisites: 1c-enterprise.a 6; A1–A2: separate infobase, catalogs, references and documents; synthetic data only.
outcomes: Specify inputs/boundaries/expectations for a future change.
Accept against old and new scenarios.
sections: A consultant reproduces workflows, checks settings and explains data. Changing posting algorithms, server rights or storage structure needs the appropriate role and review. Being able to press a command is not authority to apply it. Boundaries matter as much as producing an attractive report.

Selecting Beta instead of Alpha is a settings issue: correct selection gives 75 instead of 15. Requesting period/status absent from the starter is a schema/UI change. Renaming a variant or hiding a row cannot implement it.

Turn “fix the report” into period, document set, expected sum and observed discrepancy. Removing a wrong filter may suffice; an absent model field requires a change request. Classification saves time and prevents hiding a data issue by changing formulas without investigation.

Specify which date represents a request, end-day inclusion, included statuses, empty-set behavior and retained reports. A half-open interval can include the start and exclude the day after the end; agree meaning before implementation. This describes a future change, not a starter-report control.

Provide a minimal synthetic set, versions, steps, expected/actual and tested hypotheses. State prohibited actions: overwriting source, using real data or running unknown processors. The recipient needs a concrete task, not unsorted screenshots. Retain failed attempts to avoid repeating unsafe experiments.

Provide the synthetic 30/45/15 set, actual identities, current schema/version and expected membership. State constraints: preserve source work, retain requests, keep access controls and use no real data. Engineering verifies code/tests; the consultant retains the user question and independent reconciliation.

After a fix, the consultant repeats the user workflow and reconciliation; the developer confirms technical checks. A closed ticket is not full acceptance until the original issue and preservation are verified. Outcomes can be partial: the report is fixed while multi-user rights still await a suitable test environment.

Acceptance repeats Alpha 75/Beta15 and new boundary/status cases. Report partial scope honestly: a working filter does not establish permissions or printing. A closed ticket is not acceptance. Retain source, candidate and checks separately.

lab.title: Settings or development: hand over a testable requirement
lab.environment: Own continuing service-desk copy; no real data. Studio/Sandbox optional.
steps: Select Beta 1/15 then Alpha 2/75. Record parameters and source numbers.
Specify period/status and identify their absence from current quick settings.
Specify dates/statuses/units, included identities, empty results, period boundaries, retained work and existing report.
Separate engineer code/tests from your user controls. Supply only synthetic examples, without a real-base upload.
This lab implements the requirement, not the software change. A future candidate needs old 75/15 and new-case verification.
evidence: Actual settings/identities, expected and observed results, before/after work preserved.
For unexecuted code or future behavior, explicit NOT RUN/PLANNED instead of a native PASS.
